name: Stanly Ranch, Auberge Collection
positioning: Wellness-focused ranch resort on a historic Napa Valley wine country ranch, with cottage-like guestrooms, a Halehouse spa and the Bear restaurant
best_for: Travelers who want a spa and wellbeing stay in wine country
Families wanting a Napa stay with a dedicated family pool

facts.text: Stanly Ranch is at 200 Stanly Crossroad in Napa, California, on the southern edge of Napa Valley near the Napa River.
The resort is set on a historic wine country ranch founded in 1856 by Judge Edward Stanly.
Guestrooms are cottage-like, with in-room seating areas and grand doors that open onto generous private terraces.
Designer Jen Clausen gave the rooms a modern farmhouse look with leather and oak furnishings.
Villas have two bedrooms and a gourmet kitchen.
Dinner at Bear highlights Napa Valley ingredients using techniques such as grilling and fermenting alongside more traditional preparations.
Gavel is a coffee shop serving freshly baked pastries and Sightglass Coffee roasts.
Stanly Ranch has three pools, including a family pool and the spa pool at Halehouse.
Group fitness classes, including yoga, pilates, barre and HIIT, are complimentary to in-house guests.
Stanly Ranch is a dog-friendly resort.

highlights.text: The Springhouse circuit includes a salt room, cedar sauna, hyperbaric oxygen chamber, tepidarium and cold plunge.
Stanly Ranch is a working ranch, and its menus are sustainably sourced and seasonally driven.
The concierge can arrange a helicopter tasting with Donum Estate.
Basin Bar sits between the Lavender pool and the kids pool and serves light dishes, wood fire pizzas and cocktails.

Halehouse offers individualized wellbeing programs designed by wellness specialists, medical professionals and sports experts, covering nourishment, hydration, sleep, movement and targeted treatments.

considerations.text: San Francisco Airport is about a 1 hour 20 minute drive from the resort.
Downtown Napa is about 10 minutes from the resort and Sonoma about 20 minutes.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires transportation to nearby attractions.
